subject: Airlocked site activation & artifact provenance — checklist and witness plan
messages:
From: Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@auroratech.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@auroratech.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Airlocked deployment onboarding — next steps

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Aurora is preparing an ‘airlocked’ host for Redwood’s runtime next quarter and procurement asked me to confirm two things before we proceed:

1) The exact artifact formats and signing metadata you require for on-site ingestion (we need to produce a manifest that matches your attestation checks).
2) Who from Redwood can act as a remote witness for the activation window — Aurora policy requires a named witness plus a signed activation form.

We intend to ship artifacts on encrypted physical media; procurement would prefer a clear checklist so they can scope the shipyard. Can you share your preferred manifest template and the witness process?

Best,
Sam
Sam O'Neill
Program Manager, Edge Systems
Aurora Technologies
[Attachment: initial-reqs.xlsx (32KB)]

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@auroratech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Airlocked deployment onboarding — next steps

Sam — thanks, this is helpful. High-level answers below; attaching a sample manifest and our signer instructions.

Summary (short):
- Accepted artifact container: .tar.gz (GPG-signed) with a top-level manifest.yml (YAML).
- Manifest fields: artifact_id, sha256, build_version, model_hashes, signer_key_id, signing_timestamp, provenance_url (optional).
- Signing: Redwood will provide a short-lived signing key for release day OR we can accept your site-generated key if you follow our KMS attestation steps (see attached).
- Witness: I (Rachel Kim) and Ben (Ben Carter) can be listed as Redwood witnesses; we will remote-join activation via secure Zoom + timestamped witness form.

Attachments included: artifact-manifest-example.yml, signing-key-instructions.pdf, activation-witness-form.pdf

Next steps I recommend:
1) Aurora populates the attached manifest template with one real image sample and returns it to us for pre-validation (automated checksum pass/fail).
2) Schedule a 2-hour activation window on the week of Dec 4 — we’ll reserve a signer and an operations lead.
3) Procurement coordinates courier ETA and HAZMAT/insured transfer info.

If you want, Ben can give a short walkthrough of the manifest fields — Ben, can you do 30m tomorrow?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_artifact-manifest.tar.gz (1.2MB), signing-key-instructions.pdf (240KB), activation-witness-form.pdf (48KB)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@auroratech.com>, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Airlocked deployment onboarding — next steps

Sam — quick notes from ops perspective (I ran the sample through our pre-validation harness):

- The sample manifest passed checksum verification but model_hashes had one unexpected extra entry; looks like a leftover debug artifact. Please remove any files matching pattern *.dbg or *.tmp before packaging.
- Signing: we expect a clear signature header (OpenPGP v2) and a detached .sig file alongside the .tar.gz. Our ingestion will reject inline signatures (policy).
- Media label: courier must include a machine-readable manifest (QR code or simple CSV) in the package leaflet so on-site operators can scan before insertion. This dramatically reduces human errors during ingest.

I’ve added two small changes to the manifest template (field comments). Attaching the version I tested.

Ben Carter
Lead Site Ops Engineer, Redwood
[Attachment: redwood_artifact-manifest.tar.gz (tested-v2) (1.2MB)]

From: Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@auroratech.com>
To: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@auroratech.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Airlocked deployment onboarding — next steps

Thanks all — good catches. Procurement: we will strip debug artifacts and produce a detached .sig for each payload.

Rachel — can you confirm the witness form process? Procurement needs the name + title of each Redwood witness and whether your witness signs digitally or physically on-site. Also, any specific identity verification requirements (e.g., government ID scan) we should prepare ahead of the activation?

Sam

On a separate note, we need to confirm insurance value for courier; I’ll put that on the procurement track and loop back.

[Forwarded attachment: initial-reqs.xlsx]

From: rachel_kim@redwood.ai
To: Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@auroratech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Nov 2028 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Airlocked deployment onboarding — next steps

Sam — finalizing plan below and confirming witness details.

Activation window: Dec 5, 2028 09:00–11:00 PST (proposed).
Redwood witnesses:
- Rachel Kim — Sr. PM, Private Deployments (will join Zoom and sign the activation-witness-form digitally).
- Ben Carter — Lead Site Ops Engineer (remote witness and will perform the post-ingest verification).
- Markus Klein — Security Review Lead (available as escalation contact and will counter-sign the activation form if required).

Identity verification: Redwood requires a single government ID scan for signatory at the courier handoff (we will accept notarized copies if Aurora policy requires). For remote witnesses we will record the Zoom session and embed the meeting ID/time into the signed activation form for audit purposes.

Deliverables we will validate on-site during activation:
- GPG detached signature (.sig) verified against the signer_key_id in manifest.yml.
- All checksums (sha256) match the manifest entries.
- No disallowed files (*.dbg, *.tmp) are present.
- Operator-scanable manifest label matches the included manifest.

Attachments: activation-witness-form.pdf (filled template), redwood_artifact-manifest-tested-v2.tar.gz

I’ll open a short JIRA ticket for the activation runbook (ENGINF-824) and share the checklist with procurement. Thanks for moving quickly on this — these checks should keep the run smooth and auditable.

Rachel

--
Rachel Kim
